html:
The Mvskoke, or Muscogee, called Creek by the English, are a Native people of what are now Georgia and Alabama. They descend from the Mississippian chiefdoms of the Southeast, whose towns De Soto's army passed through in 1540.

By the 1700s they formed a confederacy of independent towns, Upper Creeks on the Coosa and Tallapoosa rivers and Lower Creeks on the Chattahoochee, joined by peoples such as the Hitchiti and the Koasati. They farmed maize, hunted deer and traded skins with the English, French and Spanish. Some moved south into Florida and became part of the Seminole.

A civil war among the Creeks grew into the Creek War of 1813 and 1814, which Andrew Jackson ended at the Battle of Horseshoe Bend. In the 1830s the United States forced most Muscogee to Indian Territory along the Trail of Tears. In 2020 the Supreme Court ruled in McGirt v. Oklahoma that their reservation in Oklahoma had never been dissolved. See also Muskogee.
